model: Automatic Navigation PV Module Mounting Robot (MMR)
name: Leapting PV module mounting robot
specialisedFor: utility-scale solar construction: lifting PV modules and placing them on tracker racking
summary: Tracked, self-navigating robot that carries a tray of solar modules, finds the racking with AI vision and places each module with an arm, about one module per minute. Used on the Culcairn solar farm in Australia and contracted for fully robotic module installation in Saudi Arabia.

germany.statusNote: No German or European seller, project or price found. Leapting sells from Shanghai (sales@leapting.com on its site); the projects read are in Australia and Saudi Arabia.

specs.label: Installation rate
specs.conditions: maker figure, one module per minute
specs.quote: the robot is capable of installing 60 modules an hour or one per minute

specs.label: Heaviest module
specs.quote: It can lift modules weighing up to 30 kilograms

specs.label: Chassis
specs.value: caterpillar tracks with automatic navigation and obstacle avoidance, module tray and robot arm
specs.quote: The machine features a caterpillar-track chassis, fully automated navigation and obstacle avoidance systems, and is equipped with a solar panel tray. It uses a robotic arm to pick up and place solar panels onto solar brackets.

specs.label: Speed vs. manual
specs.value: 3-5 times a worker's 90-120 modules per 8-hour day
specs.quote: within an 8-hour workday, LEAPTING says a single worker can install approximately 90-120 modules daily, while the robot’s installation efficiency increases by 3-5 times

specs.label: Claimed installation cost saving
specs.quote: delivering an estimated 30% reduction in installation costs on utility-scale solar projects

notes: High-passability tracked chassis for complex outdoor terrain (maker).
AI vision finds the brackets and their position relative to the torque tube; the robot detects module placement and rotation angles and aligns to the rack tilt.
Number of modules on the tray not stated; armPayloadKg is the heaviest module named.

evidence.task: Installs PV modules on the trackers of a utility-scale solar farm under construction

evidence.note: Leapting's first commercial project in Australia; operations were due to start in mid-February 2025.

evidence.task: Ten robots to install all of the more than 149,000 modules of a 105 MWp fixed-tilt project
evidence.where: Aloy Charge PPA project, Saudi Arabia
evidence.note: Contract signed; robot deployment scheduled for Q1 2026.
